title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its stance on how AI should be governed in the public sector. It emphasizes the need for clear, transparent guidelines, collaboration across stakeholders, and measures to protect public interest while encouraging responsible AI innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has issued a policy outlining how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications to keep exams fair, transparent, and trustworthy. The plan calls for clear guidelines, risk‑assessment procedures, and collaboration with education and industry partners to manage AI’s impact on assessment quality.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are used when training AI systems and evaluates the legal and economic effects of this practice. It also provides recommendations to balance creators' rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a formal response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, addressing the report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It stresses the need for regulatory action, investment in AI, and safeguarding public interests while encouraging innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document lays out the terms of reference for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence affects public standards, and it includes FAQs to explain the committee’s scope and purpose. The committee will examine AI’s alignment with public norms, focusing on transparency, accountability, and inclusiveness.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee about how artificial intelligence should be governed. The submission outlines the organisation’s views and recommendations for the committee’s inquiry into AI governance.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products, making sure they remain safe and effective. It also lays out how to apply the principles from the AI White Paper to update the regulatory framework for devices and drugs.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a vision to make our defence organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user for a country of our size. It outlines how we will develop, deploy, and govern AI responsibly across all defence operations to support national security objectives.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport artificial intelligence action plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness AI benefits while controlling associated risks. It outlines strategies, collaborations, and guidelines to promote safe, efficient AI integration across UK transport systems.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright-protected works are being used to train and develop AI systems, focusing on the current status under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines progress made, highlights compliance challenges, and offers recommendations for future policy and practice.
